chapter_note: This introduction is largely justificatory/editorial: Mani’s self-presentation, injunctions to record oral teaching, and comparison with earlier apostles dominate (PASTORAL/FRAME/OVERLAY). Embedded within it, however, is a relatively continuous cosmogonic survey (paras 1–9) and a brief schematic ‘three lessons’ heading (para 12) that looks like older systematic teaching language, though heavily lacunose. Paragraph 10 is bibliographic/canonical self-reference (later authorizing layer), not the older impersonal cosmological core.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological construction by the Living Spirit; process/structure voice (‘set in order’, ‘constructed’, ‘foundation’).

paragraphs.core_text: Underneath [ ... ... ] all of them; and also above he [ ... ... thre]e earths, they being conjoined. paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered/structural mapping elements (‘three earths’, ‘four mountains’, ‘three vessels’) and cosmos-as-bond mechanism are strong indicators of older systematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Then the Third Ambassador! [He purified the light] by his image. He became [redeemer of] all things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Named cosmic redeemer (Third Ambassador) in the cosmogonic sequence; not a Gospel-derived ‘Saviour’ citation.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] which they occur in, from the beginning [ ... ] they are mixed and joined with one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief doctrinal axiom about primordial mixture; fits the core cosmogonic discourse though very fragmentary.

Authorizing/bibliographic self-reference to Mani’s canon (‘I have written them in my books of light: The Great Gospel… Epistles… Psalms…’). This is not the older impersonal cosmological layer but a later editorial/self-legitimating frame for the compilation.
Apologetic criterion for ‘writer/teacher of truth’ plus first-person self-assertion (‘I also… I have revealed… I have given…’): legitimating rhetoric rather than cosmological mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: (6) The first great lesson [ ... ] which in the [ ... ... ] that walks in it because of the twelve [ ... ... ] in it, which in the cities and the dwelling places found in the [ ... ] because of the doors that are opened in them [ ... ... ] upon the earth, which in the four corners [ ... ... ... ... ... ... ]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the autobiographical/personalizing tail (‘and my pains… my afflictions… suffices for the person… wise person’) as a later rhetorical application to Mani’s experiences rather than the schematic lesson-structure itself.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying schematic/numbered correspondential structure (twelve…, doors, four corners) looks like older systematic teaching, but the paragraph is heavily lacunose and has been blended with later first-person exhortation.
Institutional/community instruction about recording homilies and lessons; explicit ‘elect and catechumens’ marks later church operational layer.
Direct admonition to remember/write teachings; hortatory second-person voice, not cosmological exposition.
Pastoral distribution by audience categories (‘elect’, ‘suckling babes’, polemic against sects/heresies) and self-testimony; not the impersonal core register.

Too fragmentary to extract a secure core segment; the surviving language is largely about apostles/fathers, scriptures, church, and books—i.e., later legitimating/Christianizing discourse rather than systematic cosmology.
Explicit Jesus-on-earth narrative (‘Jesus trod… land of the west… his parables… signs and wonders… wrote a book’): enters via Christian/Gospel tradition, hence overlay.
Comparative apostolic biography about Zarathustra not writing books; serves the justificatory frame for Mani’s own writings rather than presenting cosmological mechanics.
Parallel justificatory anecdote about Buddha and disciples writing later; functions as editorial argument for textual preservation.
General institutional warning about church decay and adulteration of teaching if not written; hortatory and community-facing.
Commandments/scriptures and ‘write after me so that it leads you not astray’—operational instruction; mixed with church vocabulary.
Continues exhortation to remember and write portions of oral teaching; not cosmological.
Closing encouragement about the benefit/enlightening effect of writing; epilogic framing rather than core teaching.
